merges.sentence: Students must not use generative AI for any work in the course.
merges.why: All state a blanket ban on AI for all coursework at every stage.

merges.sentence: Students must not use AI unless and only as the instructor explicitly authorizes.
merges.why: All make AI off-limits by default, allowed only for instructor-authorized uses.

merges.sentence: Students may use AI where the course or instructor permits it.
merges.why: All grant permission to use AI wherever course rules allow it.

merges.sentence: Students may use AI where the instructor permits it, with disclosure or attribution.
merges.why: Same permission conditioned on instructor approval plus attribution.

merges.sentence: Students may use AI if they document, cite or disclose the use as required.
merges.why: All permit AI use on the condition that it is documented and credited.

merges.sentence: Students follow the AI rules their instructor sets for each course and assignment.
merges.why: All ask students to comply with the course- or instructor-set AI rules.

merges.sentence: Students follow the university's academic integrity policy, honor code and conduct rules when using AI.
merges.why: All require AI use to comply with existing institutional integrity and conduct policies.

merges.sentence: Students use AI ethically and responsibly.
merges.why: All state the same general expectation of ethical, responsible AI use.

merges.sentence: Students ask their instructor when unsure whether or how AI use is allowed.
merges.why: All direct students to clarify unclear AI rules with the instructor.

merges.sentence: AI rules differ across courses and instructors, so students check each course's expectations.
merges.why: All state that AI policies vary by course and instructor.

merges.sentence: AI permission in one course or assignment does not apply elsewhere.
merges.why: Both say a course's AI permission does not carry over.

merges.sentence: Students read the syllabus and assignment instructions to learn what AI use is allowed.
merges.why: Both ask students to check course documents for AI rules.

merges.sentence: Students cite or attribute AI-generated content and AI tools they use, like any other source.
merges.why: All require proper citation or attribution of AI use.

merges.sentence: Students disclose their AI use in a statement describing how, where and why they used it.
merges.why: All require a disclosure explaining how AI was used in the work.

merges.sentence: Students do not submit AI-generated content without acknowledging or citing it.
merges.why: All prohibit presenting AI content without attribution.

merges.sentence: Presenting uncited or undisclosed AI content as one's own is plagiarism or an integrity violation.
merges.why: All classify unattributed AI use as an academic integrity violation.

merges.sentence: Unauthorized AI use is academic misconduct, cheating or dishonesty.
merges.why: All label unauthorized or prohibited AI use as misconduct.

merges.sentence: Students verify AI output before relying on, using or submitting it.
merges.why: All require checking AI output for accuracy before use.

merges.sentence: Students check that sources and citations produced by AI exist and are accurate.
merges.why: All require verifying AI-supplied sources and citations.

merges.sentence: AI output can be inaccurate, biased or fabricated, and students should be aware of this.
merges.why: All convey the same fact about AI errors and bias.

merges.sentence: AI output can use sources without citation, risking plagiarism and false attribution.
merges.why: Both state AI output can plagiarize or misattribute sources.

merges.sentence: Students are responsible for the accuracy and content of AI-assisted work they submit.
merges.why: All place responsibility for submitted AI-assisted content on the student.

merges.sentence: Students submit only work that is entirely their own.
merges.why: Both require submitted work to be the student's own.

merges.sentence: Even when AI is allowed, students remain primary authors of their ideas, analysis and final work.
merges.why: All require the core ideas and final work to stay the student's own despite AI use.

merges.sentence: Students understand everything they submit and do not submit AI output they do not comprehend.
merges.why: Both require comprehension of submitted content.

merges.sentence: Students can explain and defend their submitted work when asked.
merges.why: Both expect students to explain and defend their work.

merges.sentence: Students use AI to support their learning, not as a shortcut or replacement.
merges.why: All frame acceptable AI use as supplementing, not replacing, learning.

merges.sentence: Students must not use AI to replace their own thinking, effort or learning.
merges.why: All prohibit AI substituting for the student's own thinking and learning.

merges.sentence: Students ask themselves whether their AI use supports or undermines their learning.
merges.why: All ask students to reflect on whether AI use serves their learning.

merges.sentence: Students make informed choices, weighing benefits and risks, about when and how to use AI.
merges.why: Both ask for deliberate judgment before using AI.

merges.sentence: Students consider the environmental and ethical impacts of their AI use.
merges.why: All ask students to weigh AI's environmental and societal costs.

merges.sentence: Students may use AI to brainstorm and generate ideas.
merges.why: All permit or endorse AI for brainstorming.

merges.sentence: Students may use AI as a personal tutor or study aid.
merges.why: Both describe AI as a tutor for students.

merges.sentence: Students may use AI to summarize readings and sources.
merges.why: Both permit AI summarization of readings.

merges.sentence: Students must not use AI summaries in place of doing the readings.
merges.why: Both prohibit substituting AI for doing the reading.

merges.sentence: Students may use AI to summarize readings only with instructor permission.
merges.why: Both make AI summarization conditional on instructor approval.

merges.sentence: Students may use AI to revise and edit their own drafts.
merges.why: Both permit AI-assisted revision of one's own drafts.

merges.sentence: Students may use AI to raise counterarguments and gaps in their own thinking.
merges.why: Both permit AI as a critic surfacing objections.

merges.sentence: Students do not use AI to draft, edit, revise or proofread their work.
merges.why: All prohibit AI for writing and editing one's work.

merges.sentence: Students must not use AI writing assistants such as Grammarly in coursework.
merges.why: Both put AI editing tools like Grammarly under the restriction.

merges.sentence: Students must not use AI to generate content for, or include AI output in, their assignments.
merges.why: All prohibit AI-generated content in submitted work.

merges.sentence: Students must not use AI to complete assignments or assessments meant to show their own understanding.
merges.why: Both prohibit AI completing the assessed task.

merges.sentence: Students do not use unauthorized AI during exams, quizzes or tests.
merges.why: Both prohibit unauthorized AI during exams.

merges.sentence: Students submit their AI prompts and outputs or chat transcripts with their work.
merges.why: All require submitting the AI interaction record.

merges.sentence: Students may be required to submit their prompts, transcripts or AI documentation.
merges.why: Both say instructors may ask for AI process records.

merges.sentence: Students keep their prompts, chats and AI use logs and be ready to provide them.
merges.why: Both require retaining records of AI use.

merges.sentence: Students reflect in writing on their AI use and its effect on their learning.
merges.why: Both require a reflection on AI use and learning.

merges.sentence: Students clearly identify which parts of their work AI generated.
merges.why: Both require marking AI-generated portions.

merges.sentence: Students identify the specific AI tool, provider, version and access date in disclosures.
merges.why: Both require naming the specific tool used.

merges.sentence: Students consult guidance on how to cite or disclose AI use.
merges.why: Both direct students to citation guidance for AI.

merges.sentence: Students follow their instructor's requirements for citing and disclosing AI use.
merges.why: Both defer AI disclosure format to instructor requirements.

merges.sentence: Students honestly explain their AI use when asked.
merges.why: Both require honest accounts of AI use on request.

merges.sentence: By submitting work, students attest it is their own original work.
merges.why: All treat submission as a claim of sole authorship.

merges.sentence: Students treat AI like help from another person under existing plagiarism and integrity rules.
merges.why: All apply human-assistance rules to AI.

merges.sentence: Students get advisor or committee approval before using AI in theses or research.
merges.why: Both require advisor approval for AI in research.

merges.sentence: Graduate students discuss their AI use with their advisor or committee.
merges.why: Both ask students to discuss AI use with advisors.

merges.sentence: Students seek help from instructors, librarians, writing centers and tutoring.
merges.why: Both direct students to human support resources.

merges.sentence: Students learn to use AI because it prepares them for their careers.
merges.why: Both justify learning AI as career preparation.

merges.sentence: Students build skills to use AI effectively, an important emerging skill.
merges.why: Both treat AI proficiency as a skill to develop.

merges.sentence: The course's competencies prepare students for future careers.
merges.why: Both justify course skills as workplace preparation.

merges.sentence: Students master fundamentals without AI before using it.
merges.why: All sequence AI use after foundational skills.

merges.sentence: Group members agree on AI use together and disclose it to the instructor.
merges.why: Both require group agreement and transparency on AI use.

merges.sentence: Students need not disclose routine or embedded AI uses such as spell-check or autocomplete.
merges.why: All exempt routine AI features from disclosure.

merges.sentence: Students may use basic spelling and grammar tools, which are not counted as generative AI.
merges.why: Both allow basic spell and grammar checkers outside the AI rules.

merges.sentence: AI use is optional; students may choose not to use or pay for it.
merges.why: Both make AI use optional for students.

merges.sentence: Students stay informed of updates to AI guidance and policies.
merges.why: Both ask students to keep checking current AI guidance.

merges.sentence: Students use guides, tutorials and training to build AI literacy.
merges.why: Both direct students to AI literacy training.

merges.sentence: Students do not use AI to fabricate data, citations or evidence.
merges.why: Both prohibit AI fabrication of evidence.

merges.sentence: Students' AI use must be fair to peers and not give unfair advantage.
merges.why: Both ground AI use in fairness to peers.

merges.sentence: Students do not present AI-translated text as their own original work.
merges.why: Both prohibit passing off AI translation as one's own.

merges.sentence: AI cannot be credited as an author.
merges.why: Both deny AI authorship.

merges.sentence: Students are expected to use AI tools in this course.
merges.why: Both state students are expected to use AI.

merges.sentence: AI can support and improve students' learning and work.
merges.why: Both state AI's learning benefit.

merges.sentence: Students use AI in course assignments as the instructor specifies.
merges.why: Both describe AI integrated into coursework.

merges.sentence: Not knowing or not asking about AI rules is no excuse for a violation.
merges.why: Both deny ignorance of rules as an excuse.

merges.sentence: Students revise and adapt AI output rather than pasting it into their work as-is.
merges.why: All forbid submitting raw AI output unchanged.

merges.sentence: Students must not present AI-generated work as their own.
merges.why: All prohibit passing off AI output as the student's own work.
